ALL_COURSES.blurb: Redesign flux without changing the genome.
ALL_COURSES.name: Metabolic Engineering

ALL_COURSES.blurb: Shape the cell from within during mitosis.
ALL_COURSES.name: Morphogenesis Laboratory

bacterivore.blurb: Active hunting. High pay; you also eat while working.
bacterivore.name: Bacterivore Security Agency

detritus.blurb: Decomposer work. Steady pay but raises Cellular Stress / toxins.
detritus.name: Detritus Processing Corp

solar.blurb: Photosynthesis shifts. Pays best on Sunny cycles; cloudy days hurt.
solar.name: Photic Solar Plant

choices.desc: Burn ATP to silence the foreign transcripts.
choices.label: Fire up RNA interference (siRNA)
choices.result: The phage gene expression is silenced. Integrity +4, stress −4.

choices.label: Shed the affected membrane patch
choices.result: You vesiculate the receptor and escape. −6 μg C.

choices.label: Ignore it and keep working
choices.result: Lysogeny pressure costs you: stress +22 and −10 size.

EVENTS.prompt: A tailed bacteriophage lands on your membrane and begins to inject its genome.
EVENTS.science: Many protists (Tetrahymena, Paramecium) carry RNA interference machinery that silences viral and transposable transcripts; apoptosis-like programmed cell death also exists in unicellular eukaryotes.
EVENTS.title: Viral Particle Adsorption

EVENTS.prompt: A lysed neighbour releases a cloud of amino acids and sugars right beside you.
EVENTS.science: Saprotrophy — absorbing dissolved organic matter — is common in protists and bacteria.
EVENTS.title: Nutrient Windfall

EVENTS.prompt: Dilute rainwater floods your patch of biofilm.
EVENTS.science: Freshwater protists use contractile vacuoles to expel water and avoid lysis.
EVENTS.title: Osmotic Downpour

choices.label: Secrete a mucilage cyst
choices.result: You survive, but lose time: −18 ATP, stress −6.

EVENTS.prompt: A water bear grazes through the biofilm, sweeping up everything in its path.
EVENTS.science: Tardigrades are micro-predators of protists; mucocysts and trichocysts are defensive exocytoses.
EVENTS.title: A Tardigrade Approaches

choices.label: Exploit the public goods without signalling
Relay the signal to the rival

EVENTS.prompt: Autoinducer molecules ripple across the biofilm: the population is talking.
EVENTS.science: Quorum sensing lets microbes coordinate gene expression by population density.
EVENTS.title: Quorum Sensing Wave

choices.label: Synthesise protective pigment
choices.result: Pigment laid down. −18 μg C, signaling +2, stress −3.

choices.desc: Chloroplasts love it; DNA does not.
choices.label: Stay in the light

EVENTS.prompt: The biofilm thins overhead and harsh UV-B reaches your cell.
EVENTS.science: UV causes pyrimidine dimers; photolyases and nucleotide-excision repair fix them.
EVENTS.title: Ultraviolet Pulse

choices.label: Clear the traffic with a training session

EVENTS.prompt: Kinesin traffic jams on your microtubules; vesicles pile up in the cytoplasm.
EVENTS.science: Intraflagellar transport and kinesin/dynein traffic can be impaired by oxidative stress.
EVENTS.title: Motor Protein Jam

choices.label: Adapt your phenotype to the silenced state
choices.result: Stress +8, but size +3 as resources reroute.

EVENTS.prompt: Chromatin condenses unexpectedly and part of your expressed programme goes quiet.
EVENTS.science: Histone deacetylation and DNA methylation silence genes without changing their sequence — plasticity's dark side.
EVENTS.title: Epigenetic Silencing

EVENTS.prompt: A colony invites you to settle into its matrix.
EVENTS.science: Extracellular polymeric substances hold biofilms together; residents gain protection and lose mobility.
EVENTS.title: Biofilm Recruitment

EVENTS.prompt: The cell beside you divides, blasting its daughters into your space.
EVENTS.science: Crowding changes local nutrient and oxygen availability — a real density-dependent cue.
EVENTS.title: Mitotic Neighbour

choices.label: Run your hydrogenosomes
choices.result: ATP +12, stress −6. H₂ bubbles off harmlessly.

choices.desc: Inefficient without oxygen, but keeps the membrane potential.
choices.label: Push aerobic respiration harder

choices.desc: Slow everything down and wait for oxygen.
choices.label: Enter metabolic torpor

EVENTS.prompt: You drift into a dense, O₂-depleted corner of the biofilm. Aerobic respiration stalls.
EVENTS.science: Hydrogenosomes and mitosomes are mitochondrion-related organelles of anaerobic eukaryotes; hydrogenosomes make ATP by substrate-level phosphorylation and release H₂.
EVENTS.title: Anoxic Pocket

boutique.blurb: Synthesise permanent organelles: appliances, vehicles, armour.
boutique.name: Golgi & ER Boutique

detritus.blurb: Decomposer work. Steady pay, rising oxidative stress.
detritus.name: Detritus Processing Corp

diner.blurb: Immediate nutrition and bulk stock for your storage granules.
diner.name: Phagosome Diner

gym.blurb: Train motility & integrity. Flush oxidative stress and waste.
gym.name: Cytoskeleton Gym & Lysosome Spa

home.blurb: Rest safely, review your organelles, express your phenotype.
home.name: My Cell Interior

rift.blurb: Signal, cross-feed, deter or prey on the rival.
rift.name: Quorum-Sensing Rift

security.blurb: Active hunting/phagocytosis. High pay, needs lysosomes.
security.name: Bacterivore Security Agency

trophic.blurb: The district's job board — careers happen in their own workplaces.
trophic.name: Trophic Labour Exchange

university.blurb: Three majors. Transcribe gene programmes from Tier 1 to 4.
university.name: Ribosome & Nucleus University

basal.name: Basal Bodies
basal.science: Kinetosomes nucleate axonemes — the anchor for every cilium and flagellum.

chloroplast.name: Chloroplast
chloroplast.science: Euglena's secondary-endosymbiont plastid fixes carbon from light.

cilia.name: Coordinated Cilia
cilia.science: Metachronal waves of 9+2 axonemes; needs cytoskeletal engineering.

eyespot.effect: +10% solar pay: you aim your chloroplasts at the light.
eyespot.name: Eyespot (Stigma)
eyespot.science: Carotenoid granules shade the paraflagellar photoreceptor — phototaxis.

flagellum.name: Whip Flagellum
flagellum.science: A long undulating axoneme with intraflagellar transport — pure speed.

frustule.effect: Glass armour: blocks hazards and raids, −2 stress each cycle, +6 integrity.
frustule.name: Silica Frustule
frustule.science: Precipitated SiO₂ valves (epitheca + hypotheca) with nanoporous areolae.

holdfast.effect: METAMORPHOSIS: settle and anchor. +35% pay, +25% travel cost. Irreversible!
holdfast.name: Holdfast (Settlement)
holdfast.science: The posterior holdfast adheres the trumpet ciliate to a substrate.

hydrogenosome.effect: Anaerobic ATP: in Anoxic cycles you gain +10 ATP instead of −10. Also −4 stress in Anoxic.
hydrogenosome.name: Hydrogenosomes
hydrogenosome.science: Mitochondrion-related organelles (Trichomonas, rumen ciliates, anaerobic fungi) that make ATP by substrate-level phosphorylation and release H₂ and acetate — no O₂ needed.

lysosome.effect: Required for Bacterivore hunting. −3 stress per detritus shift.
lysosome.name: Lysosome Battery
lysosome.science: Acid hydrolases digest what the phagosome delivers.

macronucleus.effect: Somatic genome powerhouse: +5% pay. Upkeep 4 μg C/cycle.
macronucleus.name: Macronucleus
macronucleus.science: Polyploid nucleus runs everyday gene expression.

micronucleus.effect: Germline reserve: +3 signaling. Upkeep 4 μg C/cycle.
micronucleus.name: Micronucleus
micronucleus.science: Diploid germline nucleus divides by mitosis; stays silent otherwise.

myoneme.effect: Escape contraction: blocks hazards & rival raids. +5 max ATP.
myoneme.name: Myoneme Spring
myoneme.science: Spasmoneme: a Ca²⁺-driven protein spring contracts in milliseconds.

oral.effect: +20% nutrition from food; counts as phagocytic apparatus.
oral.name: Oral Groove
oral.science: Ciliated groove sweeps bacteria into the cytostome.

pellicle.effect: Blocks hazards, UV stress & rival raids. +3 signaling.
pellicle.name: Pellicle Armor / Mucocysts
pellicle.science: A protein-strip pellicle with mucocysts is a flexible exoskeleton.

proboscis.effect: +25% hunting pay; rival predation steals +50% more and always lands.
proboscis.name: Proboscis
proboscis.science: The extensible anterior cone of Didinium that pierces and sucks out prey cytoplasm.

pseudopod.effect: Required for Bacterivore hunting (Paramecium uses its Oral Groove).
pseudopod.name: Phagocytic Apparatus
pseudopod.science: Pseudopodia / peristome funnel & cytopharynx engulf bacterial prey.

stalk.effect: METAMORPHOSIS: lose the telotroch bonus (+25% travel) but gain +35% pay. Irreversible!
stalk.name: Stalk Secretion (Settlement)
stalk.science: The telotroch settles, resorbs its girdle and secretes a stalk.

storage.effect: Stores up to 6 nutrient units; auto-feeds you at cycle start when nutrition < 65.
storage.name: Storage Granules
storage.science: Paramylon (Euglena) / glycogen granules act as the cell's pantry — the LQ2 Fridge.

toxicyst.effect: Paralysing harpoons: predation success 85% (vs 60%), blocks raids.
toxicyst.name: Toxicysts
toxicyst.science: Didinium's toxicysts discharge toxins that immobilise Paramecium prey before ingestion.

trichocyst.effect: Explosive harpoons: block hazards and rival raids.
trichocyst.name: Trichocysts
trichocyst.science: Exocytotic defensive organelles discharge against predators.

vacuole.effect: Cancels Osmotic Shift stress and bleeds off 6% stress every cycle.
vacuole.name: Contractile Vacuole
vacuole.science: Pumps excess water out of freshwater protists, preventing osmotic lysis.

ROUTES.blurb: Enzymes, flux and yield. Each course raises all career pay by 4%.

courses.blurb: Redesign flux without changing the genome.
courses.name: Metabolic Engineering

ROUTES.name: Metabolic Biochemistry

ROUTES.blurb: Structure and motion. Each course grants +4 motility and −2% travel ATP.

courses.blurb: Shape the cell from within during mitosis.
courses.name: Morphogenesis Laboratory

ROUTES.name: Cytoskeletal Engineering

ROUTES.blurb: Control and progression. Each course grants +2 signaling and promotion eligibility.
ROUTES.name: Genetic Regulation

fresh-daughter.intro: You are a newborn daughter cell in early G1. Your sister is racing you for the same niche. Get a trophic job, build a Contractile Vacuole, keep your meters in balance and grow to mature G1 size.
fresh-daughter.name: Fresh Daughter Cell

quests.hint: Get hired at a workplace: Solar Plant, Detritus Corp or Bacterivore Agency.
quests.label: Get an entry-level trophic role

quests.hint: Eat well every cycle to grow.
quests.label: Reach mature G1 size (55%)

quests.hint: End 3 cycles in a row with Stress ≤ 35% and Nutrition ≥ 50.
quests.label: Establish homeostasis (3 steady cycles)

fresh-daughter.tagline: Just divided! Establish homeostasis before your sister cell does.

full-cycle.intro: Guide a juvenile cell through the entire cell cycle: pass the G1/S restriction point, replicate your DNA, mature in G2 with a full organelle set, and trigger mitosis at the Checkpoint Registry.
full-cycle.name: The Full Cell Cycle

quests.hint: Each protist has a unique kit.
quests.label: Complete your signature organelle set

quests.hint: Size 90%, all goals done, low stress.
quests.label: Trigger M-phase (Mitosis)

full-cycle.tagline: G1 → S → G2 → Mitosis. Divide before your rival.

plasticity.intro: The biofilm weather turns volatile: UV bursts, osmotic shocks, blooms and murk. Express the right gene pathways for the day, learn to work in more than one trophic niche and reach the Apex Producer role.
plasticity.name: Phenotypic Plasticity

quests.hint: Ribosome University — any major raises your transcription tier.
quests.label: Express Level 3 genes (Advanced Enzymatics)

quests.hint: Work in two different workplaces to exploit the weather.
quests.label: Work in 2 different trophic pathways

quests.hint: Work shifts in the career districts.
quests.label: Earn 2,000 biomass

quests.hint: Climb: Intern → Junior → Senior → Apex. Study Genetic Regulation for the top rank.
quests.label: Obtain Apex Producer role

plasticity.tagline: Survive shifting environmental cycles and climb the trophic ladder.

arc: Juvenile: a single lobose pseudopod, exploratory cytoplasm
Growing: branched pseudopodia, contractile vacuole tunes osmosis
Mature G2: enormous, food vacuoles packed with prey
amoeba.blurb: A shapeless professional predator. Amoeba extends pseudopods to crawl and to engulf, and its cell membrane is endlessly re-modelled. Slow on the map, lethal in the security agency.
amoeba.name: Amoeba
amoeba.title: The Engulfer
traits: Starts with a Phagocytic Apparatus (can hunt from turn 1)
Hunting pay ×1.2 and Detritus pay ×1.1
Crawling is slow: normal travel, no basal-body discount
Pseudopod remodelling: +3 integrity each training session

arc: Juvenile: thin silica valves begin to precipitate
Growing: areolae pattern the frustule; chloroplasts multiply
Mature G2: a heavy, beautifully armoured photosynthetic cell
diatom.blurb: A photosynthetic protist that builds itself a glass house. The silica frustule is armour, but it is heavy: diatoms sink and move slowly. The Solar Plant loves them.
diatom.name: Diatom
diatom.title: The Silica Architect
traits: Starts with a Chloroplast (Solar Plant unlocked)
Silica Frustule blocks hazards and bleeds stress each cycle
Solar pay ×1.2; heavy cell −10% travel efficiency
High structural integrity (+8) but low motility

arc: Juvenile: two ciliary girdles, a small proboscis
Growing: toxicysts dock around the cytostome
Mature G2: a fully armed hunting barrel — the wolf of the biofilm
didinium.blurb: A barrel-shaped ciliate that hunts other ciliates. A sharp proboscis and toxicysts paralalyse prey — Paramecium is its favourite meal. It is the apex predator of the protist world, and it knows it.
didinium.name: Didinium
didinium.title: The Ciliate Wolf
traits: Starts with a Toxicyst battery (predation success 85%)
Hunting pay ×1.25; predation on the rival steals more
Fast swimmer: −5% travel cost
No chloroplast, no phagocytic funnel needed: the proboscis is the weapon

arc: Juvenile: proplastids, a single whip, a tiny eyespot
Growing: chloroplasts mature, paraflagellar body orients to light
Mature G2: paramylon stores fill; mixotrophic synergy
euglena.blurb: A flagellated cell that can photosynthesise or eat. Its phenotype is plastic: the same genome expresses a chloroplast-driven or a phagotrophic programme depending on the weather and the career you choose.
euglena.name: Euglena
euglena.title: The Mixotrophic Switcher
traits: Only specimen with a Chloroplast (unlocks Photic Solar Plant)
Phenotype switch (Photo ⇄ Hetero) costs just 4 ATP at home
Solar shifts also feed the cell (+6 nutrition)
Mixotroph synergy: +10% pay with chloroplast + phagocytic apparatus

arc: Juvenile: ciliary rows established, oral groove functional
Growing: macronucleus polyploidy rises; micronucleus held in reserve
Mature G2: trichocysts docked, conjugation-ready (but we only divide!)
paramecium.blurb: A highly motile, structurally complex ciliate. Two kinds of nuclei, defensive trichocysts and an oral groove demand upkeep — but reward the cell with speed and efficiency.
paramecium.name: Paramecium
paramecium.title: The Ciliated Executive
traits: Starts with Oral Groove: +20% nutrition from all food
−10% travel cost; high base motility
Nuclear upkeep: 4 μg C per nucleus each cycle (or −8 ATP)
Trichocysts block hazards and rival raids

arc: Juvenile: motile, searching for a substrate
Growing: secretes a holdfast and unfurls its trumpet crown
Mature: blue-green pigment protects it from light damage
stentor.blurb: A giant trumpet ciliate that anchors with a holdfast and fans a crown of cilia to filter food. Stentor is famous for regenerating from fragments — here, from physiological stress.
stentor.name: Stentor
stentor.title: The Trumpet Regenerator
traits: Holdfast settlement: +35% pay but +25% travel cost
Regeneration: −4 extra stress every cycle
Trumpet crown filters food: +15% nutrition
Blue-green stentorin pigment: High UV costs less stress

arc: Telotroch: barrel-shaped swimmer with an aboral ciliary girdle (fast!)
Settlement: attaches, loses girdle, secretes a stalk
Mature: myoneme spring snaps the zooid away from danger
vorticella.blurb: Born as a free-swimming telotroch, it must eventually settle, secrete a stalk and grow a spring-loaded myoneme. Settling is irreversible metamorphosis: you trade mobility for high earning power.
vorticella.name: Vorticella
vorticella.title: The Morphogenetic Settler
traits: Telotroch (unsettled): −25% extra travel cost
Settled (Stalk): +35% pay but +25% travel cost (anchored)
Myoneme escape-contraction blocks hazards and interference
No chloroplast: heterotroph only

anoxic.blurb: Dense biofilm, O₂ depleted: −10 ATP unless you run hydrogenosomes (+10 ATP).
anoxic.name: Anoxic Pocket
